rubrics.justification: The response overstates image quality and describes features not clearly supported by the image, including a distinct tightly packed ICM, cohesive circumferential TE, and thinning zona/pre-hatching appearance. The image appears less clearly expanded and more difficult to confidently call 3AA from morphology alone.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, oocyte yield, sperm parameters, BMI, diagnosis, and endometrial thickness with prognosis reasonably well, though it somewhat overinterprets low responder status and embryo quality from limited data.

The reasoning is generally logical and internally consistent, linking embryo grade and patient age to prognosis while adjusting for alcohol use and unexplained infertility. Minor issues include overconfidence in morphology and some speculative statements.

Recommendations such as single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst and counseling on alcohol reduction are guideline-concordant. PGT-A discussion is appropriately nuanced, though embryo banking and protocol suggestions are somewhat speculative from the available data.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, lifestyle counseling, and possible further testing or protocol adjustment. Some recommendations are useful but not highly individualized beyond standard IVF management.
